release.title: NodeLink v0.1.2 secure enrollment pilot
release.intended_use: Limited pilot deployment to owned Windows x64 endpoints after the sole repository owner reviewed and accepted the release evidence; this release is not approved for multi-tenant or high-availability claims.

server.deployment: Deploy source from the exact commit bound to v0.1.2 by the release workflow.

database.migration_policy: Migrations are forward-only. Public v0.1.1 databases must pass guarded schema adoption at 0001 before upgrading; never edit the revision or perform an in-place downgrade.

protocols.mixed_version_behavior: Agents advertise command-v3 and command-v2 during a staged rollout, but new deployments require command-v3; missing, unknown, and legacy-unversioned capabilities fail closed.

known_limitations: #24: Windows agent and installer artifacts are not Authenticode signed, so SmartScreen or antivirus warnings remain possible.
#66: Roles are global and clients or sites are not authorization tenants; do not market or operate this release as multi-tenant.
#84: Enrollment rate limits, counters, and metrics are process-local; no multi-worker or high-availability protection claim is made.
#125: Per-agent bearer credentials are long-lived and do not yet have automatic expiry, proof-of-possession, or loss-safe renewal.
#126: Empty deployments must bootstrap the first client and site through the existing administrative API before using enrollment.
#76: The local release drill verified the internal audit chain but had no external immutable audit-anchor receipt to cross-check.

Release governance deviation: the sole repository owner explicitly waived the runbook's independent second-operator review on 2026-07-28 because no second operator was available, accepting the increased risk of single-person evidence and release approval.
Caddy private-PKI testing had no reachable CRL or OCSP service; Windows Schannel curl required best-effort revocation while certificate-chain and hostname verification remained enabled.
The production dependency audit is clean, but nine high-severity findings remain in the dashboard development-only lint dependency graph and require reassessment by v0.1.3.
Public v0.1.1 predates explicit envelope negotiation; command-v1 below names its legacy signed-command compatibility format only for a full-stack recovery and never permits mixed-version operation.

prerequisites: Pause enrollment, command dispatch, server promotion, and external agent rollout automation.
Verify the encrypted 0001 recovery-point backup, current 0012 backup, manifests, and retained restore evidence against their immutable SHA-256 digests.
Confirm Python 3.12, PostgreSQL, command signing keys, production secrets, trusted-proxy settings, HTTPS public URL, and server-only dashboard API URL are configured.
Verify every release artifact checksum and GitHub build-provenance attestation before execution.
steps: For an unversioned public v0.1.1 database, run the guarded adoption dry run, review its exact fingerprint, stamp only through adopt_v011_schema.py, and confirm revision 0001.
Run Alembic upgrade to 0012 and confirm the startup revision guard passes before serving traffic.
Deploy the server and dashboard together from the workflow-bound v0.1.2 source commit.
Deploy the checksum-verified Windows agent or installer to one owned canary endpoint before expanding the rollout.
Keep public v0.1.1 and the failed-state backup unavailable to automatic rollout channels.
verification: Confirm Alembic current reports 0012 and health, readiness, metrics, login, and production configuration checks pass over verified HTTPS.
Confirm a single-use restricted Windows canary token permits exactly one enrollment and that a second redemption is generically rejected.
Confirm heartbeat, audit sequence, expected metric deltas, token revocation, agent revocation, and post-revocation authentication rejection.
Confirm the audit chain, restore evidence, encrypted-backup manifests, artifact checksums, SBOM, and provenance attestations.
Confirm NodeLinkAgent service and installer install, start, stop, restart, and uninstall behavior on Windows, with DPAPI-protected identity and restricted ACLs.

decision_path: Prefer a forward fix while the live database remains at 0012; public v0.1.1 is not a component-only or in-place server/database rollback target for that schema.
Redeploy v0.1.2 components only when their required 0012 schema and retained artifact digests exactly match the live deployment.
Before any schema restore, pause rollout and writers, preserve an encrypted failed-state backup, and name the decision maker and exact accepted data-loss window.
Restore the verified 0001 recovery-point backup only after explicit data-loss approval, validate it in isolation, and deploy the exact v0.1.1 server, agent, and installer together.
If the matching backup, artifact, audit, or startup verification fails, keep promotion blocked and continue with a reviewed forward fix.

security_impact.summary: v0.1.2 adds constrained, audited agent enrollment and revocation while preserving fail-closed command verification, production configuration checks, recovery evidence, and explicit pilot-only operating limits.
fixed_vulnerabilities: #128: Next.js was updated to 16.2.12 and exact Next-scoped PostCSS and Sharp overrides remove the directly applicable production dependency advisories.
Enrollment tokens now use high entropy, hash-only storage, mandatory expiry, single-use defaults, transactional redemption, restricted metadata, generic rejection, and audited revocation.
Windows agent identity is DPAPI protected with a restricted ACL, and revoked agent credentials fail authentication without exposing an oracle.
new_risks: #24 remains open because Windows artifacts are unsigned and require checksum and provenance verification.
#66 remains open because authorization roles are global rather than tenant scoped.
#84 remains open because enrollment limiting and counters are process local.
#125 remains open because agent bearer credentials are long-lived and lack automatic renewal.
The tested private-PKI deployment has no online revocation endpoint, and the local drill had no external audit-anchor receipt.
operator_actions: Because independent second-operator review was explicitly waived, the sole release operator must personally verify the complete v0.1.2 evidence index, retained digests, preflight result, and green release checks before tagging.
Use the release only for an owned, knowing Windows x64 pilot and document acceptance of unsigned artifacts and the non-multi-tenant authorization model.
Keep enrollment tokens single-use, restricted, short-lived, and transferred only through an approved secret channel.
Monitor audit-chain verification, backups, enrollment failures, revocations, and process-local counter resets throughout the pilot.
Use a forward fix by default; do not restore the 0001 recovery point without preserving failed state and explicitly accepting all post-backup data loss.
